# MEMORANDUM — Contract Review (Customer Side)

**Agreement:** Licensing and Web Site Hosting Agreement — TrueLink, Inc. (vendor) / Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. (Client)
**Reviewer:** In-house counsel, Client
**Bottom line:** Not signable as drafted. The commercial core is blank, the risk allocation is materially one-sided (uncapped Client indemnity vs. capped vendor liability, no vendor IP or performance warranty), the service levels are unenforceable, there are no data-security or data-return terms despite the fact that consumer credit files flow through the system, and Client can lose the service instantly and without cure for acts of its own broker customers. Items in Tier 1 should be treated as conditions to signature.

---

## Tier 1 — Deal issues

**1. Core commercial terms are blank / unagreed (p0031, p0033, p0043, p0045; Exhibits A & B at p0106, p0110).**
Storage, bandwidth, the Support Services period, both monthly minimums, and both fee schedules are blank or "to be agreed prior to Closing." Client would be bound to pay unspecified minimums and would have no contractual entitlement to any defined capacity. There is also a real question whether price is sufficiently definite to be enforceable.
*Fix:* Complete all blanks and execute Exhibits A and B as part of signature. Add: "No minimum fee is payable and no service commitment applies until Exhibits A and B are executed by both parties."

**2. Client grants TrueLink a worldwide right to resell and exploit borrower credit data (p0054; definition at p0015).**
Client purports to license TrueLink to "use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit, upload, display, copy and store" Credit Data — data of Client's, BNC Mortgage's, and their brokers' loan applicants. This is the single largest risk in the document: consumer credit reporting/privacy exposure, breach of Client's own reps (p0051), likely conflict with Client's investor and broker agreements, and a real question whether Client even has authority to license BNC's and brokers' applicant data. The limitation is "in accordance with the Non-Competition Agreement," which is **not defined, attached, or otherwise identified**. The definition itself is unusable — it is internally garbled and conditions the archiving date on agreement "between Client and Keith Guy," a named individual.
*Fix:* Delete Section 8(d), or narrow to a limited internal right to use de-identified, aggregated data for service operation and improvement, with express prohibitions on resale, redistribution, and any consumer-level use; require TrueLink compliance with all consumer credit reporting and privacy laws and add a TrueLink indemnity for misuse. If the license is retained in any form, define and attach the Non-Competition Agreement, rewrite the Credit Data definition, delete the reference to an individual, and expressly terminate the license (with certified deletion) on expiration or termination — note that as drafted the survival clause (p0090) makes it perpetual.

**3. No data security, breach notification, audit, or data-return obligations anywhere.**
The only data-protection provision is the daily backup covenant (p0038) — with no restoration commitment, RTO/RPO, or right to obtain backup copies. There is no security standard, no encryption, no subcontractor control or flow-down, no incident notification, no audit or regulatory-examination cooperation, and no obligation to return or delete Client data at termination. As a mortgage originator, Client also has vendor-oversight expectations from its own regulators and investors that this contract cannot satisfy.
*Fix:* Add an information security schedule: administrative/technical/physical safeguards no less protective than industry standard; encryption in transit and at rest; personnel background and need-to-know controls; no subcontracting or offshoring of Client data without prior consent, with full flow-down; security incident notification within 24–48 hours plus cooperation and remediation at TrueLink's cost; annual third-party security assessment or Client audit right; regulatory examination cooperation; records retention; and return of Client data in a usable format plus certified deletion within 30 days of termination.

**4. Liability and indemnity are structurally one-sided (p0071–p0073, p0076, p0077).**
- Client's indemnity (p0072) covers *any* Client breach, acts of *any* broker customer, anything on the Web Site, and product liability for anything transmitted from the site — and expressly applies "without regard to any knowledge limitation," which strips the "actual knowledge" qualifiers Client negotiated into its IP and malicious-code reps (p0055–p0056). It is uncapped and not limited to third-party claims.
- TrueLink's cap (p0077) limits it to 12 months of fees and, worse, is ambiguous in scope: it references only "Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11" yet sits inside the Indemnity section, so TrueLink will argue it caps its indemnity at p0073 too. Section 7 is a *Client* obligation, which shows the reference list is unreliable.
- **There is no vendor IP infringement indemnity at all**, despite this being a software license (p0022, p0029) — Client bears full third-party infringement risk on TrueLink's own product.
- No indemnification procedure (notice, control of defense, consent to settle) for either party.
*Fix:* (i) Add an uncapped TrueLink IP infringement defense/indemnity with repair-replace-refund and a termination-plus-refund remedy; (ii) delete "without regard to any knowledge limitation" and limit both indemnities to third-party claims, with a carve-out for claims caused by the indemnitee's own breach or negligence; (iii) add reciprocal indemnification procedures; (iv) make the cap mutual and clearly scoped, with carve-outs for indemnification obligations, confidentiality breach, misuse of Credit Data, security incidents, gross negligence/willful misconduct, and Client's payment obligations; (v) add a supercap (e.g., 3–5x annual fees or a fixed dollar figure) for data/privacy/security claims; (vi) add a mutual consequential-damages waiver subject to the same carve-outs.

**5. No meaningful vendor warranty; broad disclaimer (p0059, p0069, p0076).**
The only express warranties are Y2K (p0059 — now obsolete) and a self-referential "same degree of care… exercised by it for its own operations" standard (p0069) that is unmeasurable and is itself inside the liability cap. Everything else is disclaimed. TrueLink gives no warranty of conformity to specification, no non-infringement, no malicious-code warranty (though Client gives one), no security warranty, and no legal-compliance warranty — even though **TrueLink**, not Client, holds the credit repository agreements.
*Fix:* Add express TrueLink warranties: services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner in accordance with the documentation and industry standard; the Interface will perform materially in accordance with its specifications; non-infringement; no malicious code; compliance with all laws applicable to TrueLink's performance, including consumer credit reporting and privacy laws; and maintenance of the repository/System licenses necessary to deliver the service. Add a remedy (re-performance, then refund/termination). Replace or delete the Y2K clause.

**6. Instant termination of the license and hosting for third-party acts, with no notice or cure (p0078).**
Sections 2 and 3 — the license and the entire hosting service — "terminate promptly" upon (a) any act or omission by Client **or any of its customers** that causes a TrueLink default under a System or Credit Repository Agreement, or (b) "any violations or breach" of Sections 8a–8c, with no materiality threshold, no notice, and no cure right. For a lender whose origination pipeline depends on credit access, automatic shutoff triggered by a broker's conduct is a business-continuity event.
*Fix:* Convert to a suspension right limited to the affected function, exercisable only where the repository or System provider has actually demanded it, and only after written notice and a commercially reasonable cure period (e.g., 10 business days) with an obligation to cooperate in remediation. Limit Client's responsibility for broker conduct to Client's failure to implement and enforce agreed access controls. Add a materiality qualifier to the Section 8 trigger.

**7. Client has no express termination rights for TrueLink's failures, and no transition assistance.**
Section 14 (p0079) gives Client only a wind-down mechanic; there is no right to terminate for TrueLink's material breach, chronic service failure, insolvency, security incident, or loss of a repository license — and no refund. Post-termination, Client bears the entire migration burden (p0078), with inconsistent 30-day and 60-day deadlines and no obligation on TrueLink to assist or hand back data. Termination cross-references point to Section 12, which is the Indemnity section.
*Fix:* Add Client termination rights for (i) material breach with 30-day cure, (ii) repeated SLA failures, (iii) insolvency, (iv) material security or privacy breach, (v) TrueLink's loss of any System/Credit Repository Agreement, and (vi) TrueLink change of control, each with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Add a 90–180 day transition assistance obligation at then-current rates, data export in a documented usable format, and a termination-tail license if needed. Fix the cross-references.

**8. Service levels are unenforceable and there is no remedy (p0032–p0034, p0036, p0040).**
"Reasonable commercial efforts," "approximately 24 hours a day," with "normal maintenance and unforeseen hardware or communications problems excepted" — that excepts essentially all downtime. The response-time metric is a one-off Client self-benchmark of *home page load* over a 28.8K modem, which measures nothing relevant to credit pulls or underwriting submissions, and the only consequence of failure is that TrueLink will "use reasonable commercial efforts" to add bandwidth (p0033). Force majeure runs in TrueLink's favor only (p0097), with no cap and no fee relief.
*Fix:* Add a defined availability commitment (e.g., 99.5%+ monthly, excluding a capped, noticed maintenance window), transaction-level response and support response/resolution targets, service credits, and a termination right for chronic failure. Make force majeure mutual (excluding payment), require disaster recovery notwithstanding force majeure, and add fee abatement plus termination if a force majeure event exceeds 15–30 days.

---

## Tier 2 — Important commercial and legal terms

**9. Payment terms and pricing exposure (p0045, p0047).** Net 15 is short; Client must **pay** disputed amounts in order to contest them, and cannot contest the monthly minimums at all. Price protection lasts only one year (p0047) while the term auto-renews annually with just 30 days' non-renewal notice (p0078) — so renewal pricing is uncapped. Support Services pricing has no protection, and "other services" pricing is entirely open. The most-favored-rate covenant on hosting has no verification mechanism.
*Fix:* Net 30–45; permit good-faith withholding of disputed amounts without breach or suspension (escrow if needed); cap renewal increases at CPI or a fixed percentage with 60–90 days' advance notice of renewal pricing and a corresponding non-renewal window; extend price protection to Support Services; add an audit/certification right and true-up credit for the most-favored-rate covenant.

**10. License scope does not match the deal (p0022, p0026, p0027 vs. p0006–p0007).** The recitals and the indemnity assume Client's affiliates and correspondent brokers will use the Interface, but the grant runs to "Client" only with no sublicense or permitted-user right. Separately, TrueLink may unilaterally change compatibility specifications "from time to time" (p0026), which could force Client platform spend or effectively obsolete Client's access. There is no escrow or continuity right if TrueLink fails.
*Fix:* Extend the grant to Client's affiliates and authorized broker users; require 90 days' notice and no material adverse change for compatibility/spec changes, with TrueLink bearing migration cost for changes it initiates; add source code escrow or an equivalent continuity remedy.

**11. Mandatory credit report purchase (p0042).** Client "shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested" — an exclusivity/minimum-volume commitment with pricing living in an unattached side agreement, and in tension with Client's stated freedom to use alternatives (p0022).
*Fix:* Delete or make non-exclusive; condition on competitive/most-favored pricing and availability; carve out cases where Client already holds a compliant report or where the investor or borrower requires a different source. Attach the referenced Credit Bureau Agreement and reconcile it.

**12. Confidentiality gaps (p0062–p0068).** Information must be marked "Confidential" at or before delivery to qualify (p0064) — impossible for borrower data streaming through the Interface. The deemed-confidential carve-out for Client data (p0065) helps but is garbled and should be relied on cautiously. There is no confidentiality term, no need-to-know limitation, no safeguards obligation, no return/destruction duty, and the compelled-disclosure clause demands a commercially impossible "ten days' prior notice" (p0068). Note also that TrueLink's confidentiality duty is expressly subordinated to the Section 8(d) Credit Data license (p0063).
*Fix:* Exempt all data transmitted through the Interface and all borrower/loan data from the marking requirement; add need-to-know limits, a safeguards obligation, and return/destruction on termination; make protection perpetual for trade secrets and personal information; change compelled disclosure to "prompt notice to the extent legally permitted"; delete or narrow the Section 8(d) subordination.

**13. Support Services and ownership of customizations (p0043, p0063, p0065, p0029).** The support commitment is one unnamed programmer for a blank number of months, with no response times, no replacement obligation, and a blank monthly minimum payable whether used or not. Custom work product is addressed only as *confidential information*, not as intellectual property, while Section 2(d) says TrueLink retains all ownership rights in the Interface.
*Fix:* Specify the support term, hours, response/resolution SLAs, and an obligation to replace departing personnel with comparable resources subject to Client approval. Add an IP clause: Client owns Client-specific deliverables and customizations it pays for, or at minimum receives a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to them.

**14. Vendor self-help (p0058).** TrueLink may "at any time implement technical mechanisms" to prevent conduct it deems illegal, obscene, or spam — a vague standard, no notice, no proportionality, and potential service disruption.
*Fix:* Require prior written notice and an opportunity to cure where practicable; limit intervention to the narrowest scope necessary and to actual or reasonably suspected violations.

**15. Assignment and change of control (p0080).** TrueLink may assign to any "financially responsible affiliate" (undefined) without consent, and there is no change-of-control trigger — so a competitor could acquire TrueLink together with the Credit Data license and Client's borrower data.
*Fix:* Define "affiliate"; require the assignee to assume all obligations in writing; give Client a termination right on TrueLink change of control (and specifically on acquisition by a competitor); permit Client to assign in connection with a merger or sale of the relevant business.

**16. Venue and fee-shifting (p0094–p0095).** Exclusive jurisdiction in San Luis Obispo County — TrueLink's home county, not Client's (Irvine) — with a waiver of forum non conveniens. Combined with prevailing-party fees and the broad Client indemnity (which itself includes attorneys' fees), this raises the cost of any dispute for Client.
*Fix:* Move to a neutral or Client-side forum, or at minimum make venue non-exclusive / defendant's-home-forum; carve out the right to seek injunctive relief for confidentiality or IP breaches in any court of competent jurisdiction.

**17. No insurance requirement.** Nothing obligates TrueLink to carry coverage despite its custody of consumer credit files.
*Fix:* Require technology E&O/cyber liability at a level proportionate to the data volume, plus CGL and workers' comp, with certificates and 30 days' notice of cancellation.

**18. Domain name registration (p0041, p0078).** Client "retains full ownership" of domains on termination, but nothing requires that Client be the registrant of record in the first instance.
*Fix:* Require registration with Client as registrant and administrative contact, and TrueLink cooperation with transfers at no charge.

# MEMORANDUM — Contract Review (Customer Side)

**Agreement:** Licensing and Web Site Hosting Agreement — TrueLink, Inc. (vendor) / Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. (Client)
**Reviewer:** In-house counsel, Client
**Bottom line:** Not signable as drafted. The commercial core is blank, the risk allocation is materially one-sided (uncapped Client indemnity vs. capped vendor liability, no vendor IP or performance warranty), the service levels are unenforceable, there are no data-security or data-return terms despite the fact that consumer credit files flow through the system, and Client can lose the service instantly and without cure for acts of its own broker customers. Items in Tier 1 should be treated as conditions to signature.

---

## Tier 1 — Deal issues

**1. Core commercial terms are blank / unagreed (p0031, p0033, p0043, p0045; Exhibits A & B at p0106, p0110).**
Storage, bandwidth, the Support Services period, both monthly minimums, and both fee schedules are blank or "to be agreed prior to Closing." Client would be bound to pay unspecified minimums and would have no contractual entitlement to any defined capacity. There is also a real question whether price is sufficiently definite to be enforceable.
*Fix:* Complete all blanks and execute Exhibits A and B as part of signature. Add: "No minimum fee is payable and no service commitment applies until Exhibits A and B are executed by both parties."

**2. Client grants TrueLink a worldwide right to resell and exploit borrower credit data (p0054; definition at p0015).**
Client purports to license TrueLink to "use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit, upload, display, copy and store" Credit Data — data of Client's, BNC Mortgage's, and their brokers' loan applicants. This is the single largest risk in the document: consumer credit reporting/privacy exposure, breach of Client's own reps (p0051), likely conflict with Client's investor and broker agreements, and a real question whether Client even has authority to license BNC's and brokers' applicant data. The limitation is "in accordance with the Non-Competition Agreement," which is **not defined, attached, or otherwise identified**. The definition itself is unusable — it is internally garbled and conditions the archiving date on agreement "between Client and Keith Guy," a named individual.
*Fix:* Delete Section 8(d), or narrow to a limited internal right to use de-identified, aggregated data for service operation and improvement, with express prohibitions on resale, redistribution, and any consumer-level use; require TrueLink compliance with all consumer credit reporting and privacy laws and add a TrueLink indemnity for misuse. If the license is retained in any form, define and attach the Non-Competition Agreement, rewrite the Credit Data definition, delete the reference to an individual, and expressly terminate the license (with certified deletion) on expiration or termination — note that as drafted the survival clause (p0090) makes it perpetual.

**3. No data security, breach notification, audit, or data-return obligations anywhere.**
The only data-protection provision is the daily backup covenant (p0038) — with no restoration commitment, RTO/RPO, or right to obtain backup copies. There is no security standard, no encryption, no subcontractor control or flow-down, no incident notification, no audit or regulatory-examination cooperation, and no obligation to return or delete Client data at termination. As a mortgage originator, Client also has vendor-oversight expectations from its own regulators and investors that this contract cannot satisfy.
*Fix:* Add an information security schedule: administrative/technical/physical safeguards no less protective than industry standard; encryption in transit and at rest; personnel background and need-to-know controls; no subcontracting or offshoring of Client data without prior consent, with full flow-down; security incident notification within 24–48 hours plus cooperation and remediation at TrueLink's cost; annual third-party security assessment or Client audit right; regulatory examination cooperation; records retention; and return of Client data in a usable format plus certified deletion within 30 days of termination.

**4. Liability and indemnity are structurally one-sided (p0071–p0073, p0076, p0077).**
- Client's indemnity (p0072) covers *any* Client breach, acts of *any* broker customer, anything on the Web Site, and product liability for anything transmitted from the site — and expressly applies "without regard to any knowledge limitation," which strips the "actual knowledge" qualifiers Client negotiated into its IP and malicious-code reps (p0055–p0056). It is uncapped and not limited to third-party claims.
- TrueLink's cap (p0077) limits it to 12 months of fees and, worse, is ambiguous in scope: it references only "Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11" yet sits inside the Indemnity section, so TrueLink will argue it caps its indemnity at p0073 too. Section 7 is a *Client* obligation, which shows the reference list is unreliable.
- **There is no vendor IP infringement indemnity at all**, despite this being a software license (p0022, p0029) — Client bears full third-party infringement risk on TrueLink's own product.
- No indemnification procedure (notice, control of defense, consent to settle) for either party.
*Fix:* (i) Add an uncapped TrueLink IP infringement defense/indemnity with repair-replace-refund and a termination-plus-refund remedy; (ii) delete "without regard to any knowledge limitation" and limit both indemnities to third-party claims, with a carve-out for claims caused by the indemnitee's own breach or negligence; (iii) add reciprocal indemnification procedures; (iv) make the cap mutual and clearly scoped, with carve-outs for indemnification obligations, confidentiality breach, misuse of Credit Data, security incidents, gross negligence/willful misconduct, and Client's payment obligations; (v) add a supercap (e.g., 3–5x annual fees or a fixed dollar figure) for data/privacy/security claims; (vi) add a mutual consequential-damages waiver subject to the same carve-outs.

**5. No meaningful vendor warranty; broad disclaimer (p0059, p0069, p0076).**
The only express warranties are Y2K (p0059 — now obsolete) and a self-referential "same degree of care… exercised by it for its own operations" standard (p0069) that is unmeasurable and is itself inside the liability cap. Everything else is disclaimed. TrueLink gives no warranty of conformity to specification, no non-infringement, no malicious-code warranty (though Client gives one), no security warranty, and no legal-compliance warranty — even though **TrueLink**, not Client, holds the credit repository agreements.
*Fix:* Add express TrueLink warranties: services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner in accordance with the documentation and industry standard; the Interface will perform materially in accordance with its specifications; non-infringement; no malicious code; compliance with all laws applicable to TrueLink's performance, including consumer credit reporting and privacy laws; and maintenance of the repository/System licenses necessary to deliver the service. Add a remedy (re-performance, then refund/termination). Replace or delete the Y2K clause.

**6. Instant termination of the license and hosting for third-party acts, with no notice or cure (p0078).**
Sections 2 and 3 — the license and the entire hosting service — "terminate promptly" upon (a) any act or omission by Client **or any of its customers** that causes a TrueLink default under a System or Credit Repository Agreement, or (b) "any violations or breach" of Sections 8a–8c, with no materiality threshold, no notice, and no cure right. For a lender whose origination pipeline depends on credit access, automatic shutoff triggered by a broker's conduct is a business-continuity event.
*Fix:* Convert to a suspension right limited to the affected function, exercisable only where the repository or System provider has actually demanded it, and only after written notice and a commercially reasonable cure period (e.g., 10 business days) with an obligation to cooperate in remediation. Limit Client's responsibility for broker conduct to Client's failure to implement and enforce agreed access controls. Add a materiality qualifier to the Section 8 trigger.

**7. Client has no express termination rights for TrueLink's failures, and no transition assistance.**
Section 14 (p0079) gives Client only a wind-down mechanic; there is no right to terminate for TrueLink's material breach, chronic service failure, insolvency, security incident, or loss of a repository license — and no refund. Post-termination, Client bears the entire migration burden (p0078), with inconsistent 30-day and 60-day deadlines and no obligation on TrueLink to assist or hand back data. Termination cross-references point to Section 12, which is the Indemnity section.
*Fix:* Add Client termination rights for (i) material breach with 30-day cure, (ii) repeated SLA failures, (iii) insolvency, (iv) material security or privacy breach, (v) TrueLink's loss of any System/Credit Repository Agreement, and (vi) TrueLink change of control, each with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Add a 90–180 day transition assistance obligation at then-current rates, data export in a documented usable format, and a termination-tail license if needed. Fix the cross-references.

**8. Service levels are unenforceable and there is no remedy (p0032–p0034, p0036, p0040).**
"Reasonable commercial efforts," "approximately 24 hours a day," with "normal maintenance and unforeseen hardware or communications problems excepted" — that excepts essentially all downtime. The response-time metric is a one-off Client self-benchmark of *home page load* over a 28.8K modem, which measures nothing relevant to credit pulls or underwriting submissions, and the only consequence of failure is that TrueLink will "use reasonable commercial efforts" to add bandwidth (p0033). Force majeure runs in TrueLink's favor only (p0097), with no cap and no fee relief.
*Fix:* Add a defined availability commitment (e.g., 99.5%+ monthly, excluding a capped, noticed maintenance window), transaction-level response and support response/resolution targets, service credits, and a termination right for chronic failure. Make force majeure mutual (excluding payment), require disaster recovery notwithstanding force majeure, and add fee abatement plus termination if a force majeure event exceeds 15–30 days.

---

## Tier 2 — Important commercial and legal terms

**9. Payment terms and pricing exposure (p0045, p0047).** Net 15 is short; Client must **pay** disputed amounts in order to contest them, and cannot contest the monthly minimums at all. Price protection lasts only one year (p0047) while the term auto-renews annually with just 30 days' non-renewal notice (p0078) — so renewal pricing is uncapped. Support Services pricing has no protection, and "other services" pricing is entirely open. The most-favored-rate covenant on hosting has no verification mechanism.
*Fix:* Net 30–45; permit good-faith withholding of disputed amounts without breach or suspension (escrow if needed); cap renewal increases at CPI or a fixed percentage with 60–90 days' advance notice of renewal pricing and a corresponding non-renewal window; extend price protection to Support Services; add an audit/certification right and true-up credit for the most-favored-rate covenant.

**10. License scope does not match the deal (p0022, p0026, p0027 vs. p0006–p0007).** The recitals and the indemnity assume Client's affiliates and correspondent brokers will use the Interface, but the grant runs to "Client" only with no sublicense or permitted-user right. Separately, TrueLink may unilaterally change compatibility specifications "from time to time" (p0026), which could force Client platform spend or effectively obsolete Client's access. There is no escrow or continuity right if TrueLink fails.
*Fix:* Extend the grant to Client's affiliates and authorized broker users; require 90 days' notice and no material adverse change for compatibility/spec changes, with TrueLink bearing migration cost for changes it initiates; add source code escrow or an equivalent continuity remedy.

**11. Mandatory credit report purchase (p0042).** Client "shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested" — an exclusivity/minimum-volume commitment with pricing living in an unattached side agreement, and in tension with Client's stated freedom to use alternatives (p0022).
*Fix:* Delete or make non-exclusive; condition on competitive/most-favored pricing and availability; carve out cases where Client already holds a compliant report or where the investor or borrower requires a different source. Attach the referenced Credit Bureau Agreement and reconcile it.

**12. Confidentiality gaps (p0062–p0068).** Information must be marked "Confidential" at or before delivery to qualify (p0064) — impossible for borrower data streaming through the Interface. The deemed-confidential carve-out for Client data (p0065) helps but is garbled and should be relied on cautiously. There is no confidentiality term, no need-to-know limitation, no safeguards obligation, no return/destruction duty, and the compelled-disclosure clause demands a commercially impossible "ten days' prior notice" (p0068). Note also that TrueLink's confidentiality duty is expressly subordinated to the Section 8(d) Credit Data license (p0063).
*Fix:* Exempt all data transmitted through the Interface and all borrower/loan data from the marking requirement; add need-to-know limits, a safeguards obligation, and return/destruction on termination; make protection perpetual for trade secrets and personal information; change compelled disclosure to "prompt notice to the extent legally permitted"; delete or narrow the Section 8(d) subordination.

**13. Support Services and ownership of customizations (p0043, p0063, p0065, p0029).** The support commitment is one unnamed programmer for a blank number of months, with no response times, no replacement obligation, and a blank monthly minimum payable whether used or not. Custom work product is addressed only as *confidential information*, not as intellectual property, while Section 2(d) says TrueLink retains all ownership rights in the Interface.
*Fix:* Specify the support term, hours, response/resolution SLAs, and an obligation to replace departing personnel with comparable resources subject to Client approval. Add an IP clause: Client owns Client-specific deliverables and customizations it pays for, or at minimum receives a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to them.

**14. Vendor self-help (p0058).** TrueLink may "at any time implement technical mechanisms" to prevent conduct it deems illegal, obscene, or spam — a vague standard, no notice, no proportionality, and potential service disruption.
*Fix:* Require prior written notice and an opportunity to cure where practicable; limit intervention to the narrowest scope necessary and to actual or reasonably suspected violations.

**15. Assignment and change of control (p0080).** TrueLink may assign to any "financially responsible affiliate" (undefined) without consent, and there is no change-of-control trigger — so a competitor could acquire TrueLink together with the Credit Data license and Client's borrower data.
*Fix:* Define "affiliate"; require the assignee to assume all obligations in writing; give Client a termination right on TrueLink change of control (and specifically on acquisition by a competitor); permit Client to assign in connection with a merger or sale of the relevant business.

**16. Venue and fee-shifting (p0094–p0095).** Exclusive jurisdiction in San Luis Obispo County — TrueLink's home county, not Client's (Irvine) — with a waiver of forum non conveniens. Combined with prevailing-party fees and the broad Client indemnity (which itself includes attorneys' fees), this raises the cost of any dispute for Client.
*Fix:* Move to a neutral or Client-side forum, or at minimum make venue non-exclusive / defendant's-home-forum; carve out the right to seek injunctive relief for confidentiality or IP breaches in any court of competent jurisdiction.

**17. No insurance requirement.** Nothing obligates TrueLink to carry coverage despite its custody of consumer credit files.
*Fix:* Require technology E&O/cyber liability at a level proportionate to the data volume, plus CGL and workers' comp, with certificates and 30 days' notice of cancellation.

**18. Domain name registration (p0041, p0078).** Client "retains full ownership" of domains on termination, but nothing requires that Client be the registrant of record in the first instance.
*Fix:* Require registration with Client as registrant and administrative contact, and TrueLink cooperation with transfers at no charge.

---
